free_tier.stated: USD 250 in credits on signup: 'You are entitled to a Free Trial of the Services to a value of $250 for a period of thirty-one (31) calendar days'. The trial is limited to one per customer. The Kubernetes control plane is free on every cluster; worker nodes bill from USD 0.007440 an hour for 1 core, 1 GB and 30 GB of NVMe.

egress.terms: egress and ingress fees are free and unlimited, so there is no overage price

record.interface_detail: the Civo CLI is documented; a documented API for the Civo cloud platform authenticated by an API key is also published

limits.value: USD 250 of credit over 31 calendar days, one trial per customer
the managed control plane costs nothing; workers bill from $0.007440 an hour at 1 core and 1 GB

record.limits_note: the trial is 31 days and one per customer; instance quota is published only as an image and a default of 8 vCPU is reported, not documented

identity_cost.detail: a card is required and must be verified before any instance or cluster exists: 'you need a valid payment method on file at all times, and won't be able to create Kubernetes clusters or instances before your card is verified'. The signup form itself asks only for a name, an email address and a password, and virtual or prepaid cards are refused

record.confidence_note: The control plane is free on an ongoing basis.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'You are entitled to a Free Trial of the Services to a value of $250 for a period of thirty-one (31) calendar days'

quoted hourly: xSmall 1 GB/1 core/25 GB $0.007440, Small 2 GB/1 core/25 GB $0.014881, Medium 4 GB/2 cores/50 GB $0.029762, Large 8 GB/4 cores/100 GB $0.059524, Extra Large 16 GB/6 cores/150 GB $0.119048, 2X Large 32 GB/8 cores/200 GB $0.238095
quoted: 'At Civo, we offer our new customers $250 of free credit for the first month you sign up.' and 'calculated hourly, rounding up to the next full hour'

evidence.quote: Egress and Ingress fees - Free & unlimited.
Civo CLI is a tool to manage your Civo.com account from the terminal.
This is the entire API for the Civo cloud platform.

record.notes: The compute rate card is not linear in cores: Extra Large is 6 cores for $0.119048 while 2X Large is 8 cores for $0.238095, so two Extra Large instances cost the same as one 2X Large and carry 12 cores against 8. Billing rounds up to the full hour and a stopped instance still bills.

shape.note: Extra Small; $250 covers 33,600 hours of it, which is 4.6 years at one node always on

session_cap.note: no session cap; a cluster bills per worker hour until the cluster is deleted

extras.price_note: a VPS bills by the month with an hourly rate capped at the monthly figure, so the two columns answer two questions: destroying the box between runs versus keeping it up.
extras.price_basis: 10 h/day column = 300 h at the hourly rate, which is what a server destroyed between runs costs; 24/7 column = the monthly cap, because a VPS kept up all month stops at the cap. Rates re-read on the vendor pricing page on 2026-10-23.

ps.price: included in the worker size, NVMe
ps.retention: the node's lifetime; a volume survives separately

record.binding_note: the 31-day trial window and its USD 250 ceiling end evaluated offerings before any per-hour rate limit is reached.
